**NOTE 1:** This RMarkdown file reproduces all of the pre-registered analyses along with several exploratory analyses. Exploratory analyses of differential attrition are not directly reproducible as that would require use of "raw" datasets that have not been made publicly available. Please contact Calvin Lai (calvinlai@wustl.edu) if you would like access to those analyses.

**NOTE 2:** This file was adapted for public use and may contain errors. If you notice any statistical errors, missing info, or are just having trouble understanding the analyses, feel free to contact Calvin Lai (calvinlai@wustl.edu).

**NOTE 3:** To get this to run, you'll need to change "C:/Users/Calvin/Documents/Dropbox/Projects/mib/scripts/osf/data/" to your personal directory.

  
```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Package names
packages <- c("sjPlot", "reshape", "psych", "foreign", "tidyverse", "glue", "effsize", "cowplot", "lme4", "lmerTest", "corrplot", "summarytools", "ggstatsplot", "ggthemes")

# Install packages not yet installed
installed_packages <- packages %in% rownames(installed.packages())
if (any(installed_packages == FALSE)) {
  install.packages(packages[!installed_packages])
}

# Packages loading
invisible(lapply(packages, library, character.only = TRUE))
rm(list = c("packages", "installed_packages"))

#Data to load 
t1t2 <- read_csv("C:/Users/Calvin/Documents/Dropbox/Projects/mib/scripts/osf/data/cohort1-wide-t1t2.csv", guess_max = min(12000))

# Creating variable for long analyses
t1t2Long <- t1t2 %>% select(id, knowledge.t1, theories.t1, strategy_use, biasworry.t1, knowledge.t2, theories.t2, biasworry.t2, strategy_intend)
t1t2Long <- t1t2Long %>% rename(know1 = knowledge.t1, theo1 = theories.t1, worr1 = biasworry.t1, stra1 = strategy_use, know2 = knowledge.t2, theo2 = theories.t2, worr2 = biasworry.t2, stra2 = strategy_intend)
t1t2Long <- t1t2Long %>% pivot_longer(!id, names_to=(c(".value", "time")), names_pattern = "(....)(.)")


# Loading in an alternative version for some mixed models at the end of this script
# Temporary jerry-rigging to get the code  to run properly.
t1t2Long_alternative <- read_csv("C:/Users/Calvin/Documents/Dropbox/Projects/mib/scripts/osf/data/cohort1-long-t1t2.csv", guess_max = min(12000))
# Processing to handle moderator analyses
# setting Time 2 strategy perceptions to fill in for Time 1
t1t2Long_alternative <- t1t2Long_alternative %>% mutate(
  strat_know = case_when(
  is.na(strat_know) == F  ~ strat_know,
  is.na(strat_know) == T ~ dplyr::lead(strat_know, 1)),
  strat_efficacy = case_when(
  is.na(strat_efficacy) == F  ~ strat_efficacy,
  is.na(strat_efficacy) == T ~ dplyr::lead(strat_efficacy, 1)),
  strat_mot = case_when(
  is.na(strat_mot) == F  ~ strat_mot,
  is.na(strat_mot) == T ~ dplyr::lead(strat_mot, 1))
)
# moderator analyses functions
knowledgemod.lm <- function(var){
  knitr::kable(broom::tidy(lm(knowledge.t2 ~ knowledge.t1*var, data = t1t2))[4,], digits = c(0,2,2,2,3))
}
theoriesmod.lm <- function(var){
  knitr::kable(broom::tidy(lm(theories.t2 ~ theories.t1*var, data = t1t2))[4,], digits = c(0,2,2,2,3))
}
biasworrymod.lm <- function(var){
  knitr::kable(broom::tidy(lm(biasworry.t2 ~ biasworry.t1*var, data = t1t2))[4,], digits = c(0,2,2,2,3))
}
strategymod.lm <- function(var){
  knitr::kable(broom::tidy(lm(strategy_intend ~ strategy_use*var, data = t1t2))[4,], digits = c(0,2,2,2,3))
}

# Creating cohen d round function
cohensd <- function(group2, group1){
  round(effsize::cohen.d(group2, group1, na.rm = T)$estimate, 2)
}
```

```{r descriptive analyses, echo = F, warning=F} 

# Short version
library(summarytools)
t1t2Small <- t1t2 %>% select(knowledge.t1, knowledge.t2,theories.t1,theories.t2, 
                             biasworry.t1, biasworry.t2,strategy_use, strategy_intend,
                             strat_efficacy.t2, strat_know.t2, strat_mot.t2)

knitr::kable(
  descr(t1t2Small, plain.ascii = F, style="rmarkdown", stats=c("mean", "sd", "min", "max"), 
        transpose=T, order = "preserve"), 
  digits=2)

detach("package:summarytools", unload=TRUE)

temp <- cor(t1t2Small, use = "na.or.complete")
corrplot.mixed(temp,tl.pos = "lt")


# Correlation Matrices
# Function to compute p-values of correlations
# mat : is a matrix of data
# ... : further arguments to pass to the native R cor.test function
cor.mtest <- function(mat, ...) {
    mat <- as.matrix(mat)
    n <- ncol(mat)
    p.mat<- matrix(NA, n, n)
    diag(p.mat) <- 0
    for (i in 1:(n - 1)) {
        for (j in (i + 1):n) {
            tmp <- cor.test(mat[, i], mat[, j], ...)
            p.mat[i, j] <- p.mat[j, i] <- tmp$p.value
        }
    }
  colnames(p.mat) <- rownames(p.mat) <- colnames(mat)
  p.mat
}
# Function to compute df of correlations
# mat : is a matrix of data
# ... : further arguments to pass to the native R cor.test function
cor.dftest <- function(mat, ...) {
    mat <- as.matrix(mat)
    n <- ncol(mat)
    p.mat<- matrix(NA, n, n)
    diag(p.mat) <- 0
    for (i in 1:(n - 1)) {
        for (j in (i + 1):n) {
            tmp <- cor.test(mat[, i], mat[, j], ...)
            p.mat[i, j] <- p.mat[j, i] <- tmp$parameter
        }
    }
  colnames(p.mat) <- rownames(p.mat) <- colnames(mat)
  p.mat
}


# Order: time of measurement
t1t2.corrData <- t1t2 %>% select(
  knowledge.t1,  biasworry.t1, theories.t1,strategy_use, 
  knowledge.t2,  biasworry.t2, theories.t2, strategy_intend,
  strat_know.t2, strat_mot.t2, strat_efficacy.t2
)
graphnames <- c("Knowledge about Bias T1",  "Concern about Bias T1", "Malleability of Bias T1","Strategy Use T1",
                "Knowledge about Bias T2","Concern about Bias T2", "Malleability of Bias T2",  "Strategy Intentions T2", 
                "Feasibility of Strategies T2", "Motivation to Use Strategies T2", "Efficacy of Strategies T2")

# Calculating range of df
cor.dftest(t1t2.corrData)

# Creating relevant datasets for visualization
p.mat <- cor.mtest(t1t2.corrData)
t1t2.corrData <- cor(t1t2.corrData, use="pairwise.complete.obs")

colnames(p.mat) <- graphnames
rownames(p.mat) <- graphnames
colnames(t1t2.corrData) <- graphnames
rownames(t1t2.corrData) <- graphnames

# Creating figure
pdf(file = "cohort1-corrplot_keyoutcomes.pdf", useDingbats = FALSE, width = 9, height = 6.28)
col <- colorRampPalette(c("#BB4444", "#EE9988", "#FFFFFF", "#77AADD", "#4477AA"))
corrplot(t1t2.corrData, method="color", col=col(200),  
         type="upper", order="original", 
         addCoef.col = "black", # Add coefficient of correlation
         tl.col="black", tl.srt=45, #Text label color and rotation
         # Combine with significance
         p.mat = p.mat, sig.level = 0.05, insig='blank',
         # hide correlation coefficient on the principal diagonal
         diag=FALSE 
         )$corrPos -> p1
text(p1$x, p1$y, round(p1$corr, 2)) 
dev.off()
```


<span style="color: blue;">To examine the main research question, we will use repeated-measures ANOVA to examine how AWARENESS OF IMPLICIT BIAS, PERCEIVED MALLEABILITY OF BIAS, BIAS WORRY, and INTENDED STRATEGY USE change between Time 1 and Time 2. For STRATEGY USE, we will also examine the Time 2 means in isolation as the Time 1 results may not be directly comparable. </span>
  
#### **Summary** 
  
All four outcomes changed in line with what was shown in the ADL Draft Report. These analyses are redundant with what was previously reported.

##### Knowledge changed over time. 
```{r rm anova of time on knowledge} 
summary(aov(know ~ time, data = t1t2Long))
```

##### Perceived malleability of bias changed over time. 
```{r rm anova of time on theories about the malleability of bias} 
summary(aov(theo ~ time, data = t1t2Long))
```

##### Concern about bias changed over time. 
```{r rm anova of time on bias worry} 
summary(aov(worr ~ time, data = t1t2Long))
```

##### Intentions to use strategies after training differed from baseline strategy use. The average intended use was `r round(mean(t1t2$strategy_intend, na.rm = T), 2)` uses in the next week.
```{r rm anova of time on intended strategy use} 
summary(aov(stra ~ time, data = t1t2Long))
mean(t1t2$strategy_intend, na.rm = T)
```


### Secondary analyses: Moderation of intervention effects

<span style="color: blue;">To understand how the efficacy of the program changes based on characteristics of the participant, we will examine how several variables moderate changes in the key dependent variables between Time 1 and Time 2 and are related to overall mean differences in the key dependent variables:</span>
  
  NOTE: The analyses reported in these sections are the interaction coefficients of regressions with the following formula: Time 2 DV = Time 1 DV + MODERATOR + Time 1 DV * MODERATOR. If a coefficient was significant, I graphed it.



##### <span style="color: blue;">Perceived knowledge of strategies (intended strategy use only)</span><br>
**Summary**: Perceived knowledge of strategies did not moderate training effects (but will do so with mixed models)
```{r moderator analyses: strat_know.t2, echo = F} 
knitr::kable(broom::tidy(lm(strategy_intend ~ strategy_use*strat_know.t2, data = t1t2))[4,], digits = c(0,2,2,2,3))
```

##### <span style="color: blue;">Perceived efficacy of strategies (intended strategy use only)</span><br>
**Summary**: Officers who saw the strategies as more efficacious showed smaller gains between baseline usage and intentions to use strategies.
```{r moderator analyses: strat_efficacyt2, echo = F} 
knitr::kable(broom::tidy(lm(strategy_intend ~ strategy_use*strat_efficacy.t2, data = t1t2))[4,], digits = c(0,2,2,2,3))

plot_model(lm(strategy_intend ~ strategy_use*strat_efficacy.t2,data=t1t2), type="pred", 
             terms=c("strategy_use", "strat_efficacy.t2"))
```

##### <span style="color: blue;">Motivation to use strategies (intended strategy use only)</span><br>
**Summary**: Officers who have less motivation to use strategies showed larger gains between baseline usage and intentions to use strategies. From eyeballing the crosstabs, there appear to be range restriction issues which explain this effect. 
```{r moderator analyses: strat_mot.t2, echo = F} 
knitr::kable(broom::tidy(lm(strategy_intend ~ strategy_use*strat_mot.t2, data = t1t2))[4,], digits = c(0,2,2,2,3))

plot_model(lm(strategy_intend ~ strategy_use*strat_mot.t2,data=t1t2), type="pred", 
             terms=c("strategy_use", "strat_mot.t2"))
```


##### <span style="color: blue;">Years in department </span><br>
**Summary**:  For the ADL report, I used simple dummy-codes: worked >= 5 years or worked >= 10 years. It is generally best practice to analyze continuous data continuously, so I relied on that operationalization for this report.

## EXPLORATORY ANALYSES
For this section, I will focus more on summarizing via text rather than presenting results directly. If you would like to see the results yourself, I'd be happy to pull up the output!
  
#### **Summary**
  
* Evidence of attrition
* Scales were reliable
* Most session-level variables did not matter. The exception was whether or not the facilitator pair included a current or ex-member of law enforcement. Sessions with a member of law enforcement showed bigger effects.
* Measurement correspondence was important for predicting intended strategy use. Time 2 variables were more predictive than Time 1 variables. Perceptions of the strategies were also more predictive than general perceptions about bias.


#### Differential Attrition
Yes, there was evidence of differential attrition. See supplement for details.
[Analyses not included in this version of the report]

#### Internal Consistency
I examined the internal consistency of all of our major variables at Time 1 and Time 2. It's notable to me that concerns about bias was redundant with each other, even though the questions spanned race and LGBT issues. It's also notable that intentions to use strategies had high internal consistency as well (unlike T1 strategy use).

* Police Identity Centrality: `r round(psych::alpha(t1t2 %>% select(centrality1, centrality2, centrality3))$total$raw_alpha, 2)` <br>
* Expected Respect from Citizens: `r round(psych::alpha(t1t2 %>% select(respect1, respect2, respect3, respect4))$total$raw_alpha, 2)` <br>
* Knowledge of Bias T1: `r round(psych::alpha(t1t2 %>% select(knowledge_bias.t1, knowledge_race.t1, knowledge_culture.t1))$total$raw_alpha, 2)` <br>
* Knowledge of Bias T2: 
`r round(psych::alpha(t1t2 %>% select(knowledge_bias.t2, knowledge_race.t2, knowledge_culture.t2))$total$raw_alpha, 2)` 
<br>
* Perceived Malleability of Bias T1: 
`r round(psych::alpha(t1t2 %>% select(theories1.t1, theories2.t1))$total$raw_alpha, 2)` 
<br>
* Perceived Malleability of Bias T2: 
`r round(psych::alpha(t1t2 %>% select(theories1.t2, theories2.t2))$total$raw_alpha, 2)` 
<br>
* Concerns about Bias T1: 
`r round(psych::alpha(t1t2 %>% select(biasworry_black.t1, biasworry_asian.t1, biasworry_hispanic.t1, biasworry_lgb.t1, biasworry_trans.t1))$total$raw_alpha, 2)` 
<br>
* Concerns about Bias T2: 
`r round(psych::alpha(t1t2 %>% select(biasworry_black.t2, biasworry_asian.t2, biasworry_hispanic.t2, biasworry_lgb.t2, biasworry_trans.t2))$total$raw_alpha, 2)`
<br>
* Strategy Use T1: 
`r round(psych::alpha(t1t2 %>% select(substitution_use, perspective_use, exposure_use, individuation_use, mindful_use))$total$raw_alpha, 2)`
<br>
* Intentions to Use Strategies T2: 
`r round(psych::alpha(t1t2 %>% select(substitution_intend, perspective_intend, exposure_intend, individuation_intend, mindful_intend))$total$raw_alpha, 2)`
<br>
* Perceived Efficacy, Knowledge, and Motivation to Use Strategies (Composite): 
`r round(psych::alpha(t1t2 %>% select(strat_efficacy.t2, strat_know.t2, strat_mot.t2))$total$raw_alpha, 2)` 
<br>


#### Session-Level Variables
I examined whether five session-level variables predicted Time 2 knowledge of bias, concern about bias, perceived malleability of bias, and intentions to use strategies. These variables were number of attendees, facilitator gender (male-male, male-female, or female-female), facilitator race (Black-White, White-White, or Asian-Black/White; note: there were no Black-Black pairs), whether one of the facilitators was current or ex-law enforcement (10% of the sessions) or had a connection with law enforcement (e.g., family; 29-39% of sessions, depending on operationalization). Of these five variables only attendance and whether a facilitator was current or ex-law enforcement predicted outcomes.

Higher attendance very slightly predicted reduced intended strategy use only r(3355) = -.05, p = .0007.

Sessions with the three facilitators who were ex-law enforcement seemed to generate slightly larger learning effects for knowledge of bias and intentions to use strategies. No effects were observed for concerns about bias or perceived malleability of bias. (0 = no law enforcement facilitator; 1 = had law enforcement facilitator)

```{r facilitator analyses, echo=F}
ggbetweenstats(data = t1t2, x = facilduo_le, y = knowledge.t2) # LE > non-LE; p < .001, g = .23

ggbetweenstats(data = t1t2, x = facilduo_le, y = strategy_intend) # LE > non-LE; p = .002, g = .17
```


#### Mixed Models
I re-conducted our statistically significant pre-registered analyses with mixed models instead of linear regression / repeated-measures ANOVAs. The primary intervention effects replicated, but 9/13 of the significant moderator analyses did not. The 4 significant moderator analyses that did replicate with a mixed model approach involved perceived efficacy of strategies,perceived motivation to use strategies, and whether the facilitator pair had a member of law enforcement. UPDATE 21-06-07: Weirdly, knowledge of bias moderated results with a mixed model but not with regular regression.

```{r mixed models}
# Creating variable for long analyses [revised: more efficient]
t1t2Long <- t1t2 %>% select(id, knowledge.t1, theories.t1, strategy_use, biasworry.t1, knowledge.t2, theories.t2, 
                          biasworry.t2, strategy_intend, strat_know.t2, strat_efficacy.t2, strat_mot.t2, 
                          frequency_black, frequency_hispanic, frequency_asian,
                          yearsworked, race_white, race_black, facilduo_le)
t1t2Long <- t1t2Long %>% rename(strategy.t1 = strategy_use, strategy.t2 = strategy_intend, 
                              strat_know = strat_know.t2,strat_efficacy = strat_efficacy.t2, strat_mot = strat_mot.t2)

t1t2Long <- t1t2Long %>% pivot_longer(cols = ends_with(c("t1", "t2")), names_to=(c(".value", "time")), names_sep = ".t(?=\\d)")

library(lme4) # package for running mixed models
library(lmerTest) # package for getting p-values

head(t1t2Long)
```

##### Original analyses
```{r mixed models of original analyses}
knitr::kable(summary(lmer(knowledge ~ time + (1|id), data = t1t2Long))$coefficients, digits = 2)
knitr::kable(summary(lmer(theories ~ time + (1|id), data = t1t2Long))$coefficients, digits = 2)
knitr::kable(summary(lmer(biasworry ~ time + (1|id), data = t1t2Long))$coefficients, digits = 2)
knitr::kable(summary(lmer(strategy ~ time + (1|id), data = t1t2Long))$coefficients, digits = 2)
```

```{r computing cohens d}
# Officers were more likely to believe in the existence of subtle or hidden biases after taking the training (b = .68, SE = .02, t = 27.27, p < .001, d = .44). 
cohensd(t1t2$knowledge.t2, t1t2$knowledge.t1)


# They also expressed more concern about unintended biases (b = .38, SE = .02, t = 16.06, p < .001, d = .24). 
cohensd(t1t2$biasworry.t2, t1t2$biasworry.t1)

# We found very slight reductions in beliefs that bias was malleable (b = -.09, SE = .03, t = -3.20, p < .001, d = -.06), 
cohensd(t1t2$theories.t2, t1t2$theories.t1)

# Relative to their self-reported baseline usage of the five strategies, officers reported much higher intentions to use the strategies over the next week (b = 1.39, SE = .03, t = 45.22, p < .001, d = .77). 
cohensd(t1t2$strategy_intend, t1t2$strategy_use)


# The largest gains were in stereotype substitution, the strategy that was used least at baseline, (b = 1.93, SE = .04, t = 49.49, p < .001, d = 1.01). 
cohensd(t1t2$substitution_intend, t1t2$substitution_use)


# The smallest gains were in the strategies that were used most at baseline, perspective-taking (b = .85, SE = .04, t = 23.08, p < .001, d = .41), and mindfulness, (b = .87, SE = .04, t = 20.77, p < .001, d = .40).
cohensd(t1t2$perspective_intend, t1t2$perspective_use)
cohensd(t1t2$mindful_intend, t1t2$mindful_use)

```
